findings.title: plan_deck still discards the tail of long comparison facts while reporting unplaced_facts=[]
findings.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Observed on HEAD 24cae082 via the real stdio MCP, protocol 2025-06-18. plan_deck(format=deckspec, slide_budget=8, template=warm-coral) with this brief: Board decision on a fictional service pilot. Revenue rose from €10m in 2024 to €12m in 2025. Gross margin fell from 45% to 38% because service costs rose. Compare building an internal support team (€0.8m per year, launch in 6 months) with outsourcing (€0.5m per year, launch in 2 months). Recommend the internal team to retain customer relationships. Pilot starts in January 2027; CFO owns funding approval in November 2026. Include backup assumptions.
Actual slots[].facts ends the comparison at "with outsourcing (€"; the €0.5m and 2-month alternative never appear in facts or unplaced_facts. unplaced_facts is empty. A using agent following the routed facts loses the economic case.
Root: internal/deckplan/facts.go extractBriefFacts truncates every remaining long clause with TruncateBrief(c,maxFactLen=120) after only splitting and/while/whereas/but. The discarded tail is never represented. balanceFactBrackets then scans a byte-index depth array whose UTF-8 continuation bytes retain zero depths, so the Euro sign can also leave an unmatched opening parenthesis. Full Brief is echoed, but this does not make the routed-facts preservation contract true.
Related closed issues csclk.48 (long-clause loss) and gvbw8 (bracketed comparisons); this is a verified residual case after their fixes. Evidence: .claude/review-evidence/2026-10-02/plan.json and tracked audit evidence. No production change requested by this audit.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Retain the full comparison in routed facts or return every omitted span in unplaced_facts with a clear truncation finding. Never truncate within a numeric/currency token. Test long parenthesized option comparisons with € and CJK text, clauses without the four recognized conjunctions, and verify every input amount/date survives. Test bracket balancing by rune rather than uninitialized UTF-8 byte slots.

findings.title: DeckSpec planner misses explicit Compare A with B requests and recommends a single-stat slide
findings.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Real MCP plan_deck(format=deckspec, slide_budget=12) brief: Compare internal support (€0.8m per year) with outsourcing (€0.5m per year) on cost and launch speed. Recommend internal support to retain customer relationships.
Actual: 8-slide storyline cover/agenda/sections + executive_summary, stat, decision, next_steps; no comparison or option_matrix. The entire two-price comparison routes to the single-number stat slot. The explicit recommendation and its rationale are absent from all slots[].facts and unplaced_facts=[]. Spare budget exists, so this is not budget pruning.
Root: internal/deckplan/deckspec_plan.go cueOptions accepts enumerated options, options evaluated against criteria, or build/buy wording but not compare X with Y. facts.go factOption similarly omits compare/compared; extractBriefFacts excludes recommendation clauses without a number, acronym, proper noun, or recognized option token before classifyFact can route them. The numeric comparison is then classified as one metric. This frustrates the advertised brief-sensitive storyline path.
Related closed khzni and gvbw8, but this exact ordinary comparison syntax remains broken. Evidence comparison-plan.json and decimal-plan.json in .claude/review-evidence/2026-10-02.
findings.acceptance_criteria: At adequate budget, Compare X with Y/on criteria creates a comparison or option_matrix before decision, routes both alternatives intact, and carries the explicit recommended alternative plus reason to the decision slot. Include positive Compare/compare with/compared to tests and negative benchmark cases (revenue compared with plan) so benchmark facts remain metrics.

findings.title: Forced thumbnail refresh invalidates valid visual reviews because PNG metadata is hashed as pixels
findings.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Real MCP reproduction at 24cae082: render examples/semantic/qbr.yaml using render_deck_spec; render_deck_thumbnails at density=100; retain all six returned image hashes; submit_visual_review with every image (accepted). Then call render_deck_thumbnails on the SAME pptx with density=100, slide_indices=[1], force=true. Resubmit the original all-slide review. It is rejected at slides[0] as an image that does not show this deck, although slide 0 was unchanged and was not even requested in the refresh. Three force calls reproduce it.
The original QBR slide-2 PNG and all three forced PNGs decode to identical RGB pixels, SHA256 a94ec66caa1c8a57542e8bdac673755247f18dc0255bd3a58bcecd6525219bac, but have distinct file hashes because ImageMagick preserves PDF/XMP creation and modification timestamps. Do not confuse this with a visual alignment bug: PDF positions and decoded pixels ruled that initial suspicion out.
Root: internal/render/render.go pdfToPNGs (~505) preserves volatile metadata; encodeImage (~583) and CachedSlideHashes (~1023) SHA256 entire PNG bytes; storeCachePNGs (~223) removes the previous source+density cache directory; deckPNGsContext rerenders ALL slides even for a selected refresh. cmd/json2pptx/mcp_visual_review_verify.go verifyReviewImages trusts only these most recent file hashes and describes them as pixel hashes. Immutable old artifact files still exist but their provenance is discarded. This forces needless full-deck rerender/review in a normal retry workflow.
Evidence: qbr-thumbs.json, qbr-force1/2/3.json, qbr-review-after-force.json; retained transcripts in .claude/review-evidence/2026-10-02, tracked audit evidence. Renderer LibreOfficeDev 26.8.0.0.alpha0, ImageMagick via repository resolver. Scope is proven image identity/cache failure, not PowerPoint rendering fidelity.
findings.acceptance_criteria: A forced same-revision refresh must not reject an earlier legitimate review image for unchanged pixels. Canonicalize PNG metadata before identity hashing and/or retain an artifact+slide render provenance ledger across refreshes. Keep rejection of wrong-slide, foreign-deck and stale-PPTX evidence. Integration regression: full render, selected force refresh after time advances, submit retained images for all slides; verify success and no weakened provenance checks.

findings.title: Shipped QBR example mixes Q2 review, completed Q4 results and ARR versus revenue measures
findings.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

The recommended semantic authoring example examples/semantic/qbr.yaml renders cleanly and scores 99, but its evidence is internally inconsistent. Cover is Q2 FY26 / path to H2; summary says Q2 revenue grew 18% QoQ. The chart presents completed Q1–Q4 FY26 quarterly revenue [34,40,44,48], calls the Q4 launch already landed, then claims continued acceleration into H2. The chart Q2/Q1 growth is 17.65% (consistent with 18%), but future Q3/Q4 values are never marked forecast. Slide 3 calls $48M Annual recurring revenue; the chart labels the same 48 as quarterly revenue ($M) without distinguishing measures. A Q2 board deck cannot establish Q4 actuals and then discuss the coming H2 in the same fiscal year without explaining chronology.
Root: authored content in examples/semantic/qbr.yaml and the examples' semantic correctness coverage, not chart math or slide layout. Agents are explicitly encouraged to copy examples, so these labels can seed polished but misleading decks. Do not attempt a generic deterministic prose truth detector as the fix.
Evidence: qbr-validate.json no issues; qbr-score.json overall 99, gate true; rendered slide 1 and 4, OOXML text. Existing closed zvu7c corrected duplicate callouts, not period/measure consistency.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Choose a coherent as-of date and period: use historical quarters through Q2, or label Q3/Q4 forecast explicitly, or convert the whole deck to a year-end review. Distinguish ARR from period revenue. Check every title, source, KPI label, chart and closing deadline against that same chronology, and add a focused fixture-content check for the chosen labels.

qbr.spec:
# Quarterly Business Review — semantic authoring example.
#
# This compact semantic spec compiles (via internal/semantic.Compile) to the raw
# json2pptx PresentationInput model and exercises the MVP slide kinds: title,
# executive_summary, kpi_snapshot, chart_insight, decision, and closing.
meta:
  title: Q2 FY26 Business Review
  subtitle: Revenue, Retention, and the Path to H2
  archetype: qbr
  template: midnight-blue
  audience: Executive leadership team

slides:
  - kind: title
    title: Q2 FY26 Business Review
    subtitle: Revenue, Retention, and the Path to H2

  - kind: executive_summary
    title: Q2 beat plan on revenue, but SMB churn now threatens H2 retention
    takeaway: Strong top-line growth, but retention needs deliberate investment in H2.
    points:
      - Revenue grew 18% QoQ, ahead of plan.
      - Net revenue retention held at 118%.
      - SMB logo churn ticked up to 2.4%.
      - Sales cycle shortened to 41 days.

  - kind: kpi_snapshot
    title: ARR reached $48M and every metric improved except SMB churn
    takeaway: Churn is the one number moving the wrong way, and it is concentrated in SMB.
    source: Internal finance and CRM data, Q2 FY26 close
    kpis:
      - { value: "$48M", label: "Annual recurring revenue" }
      - { value: "118%", label: "Net revenue retention" }
      - { value: "41d", label: "Average sales cycle" }
      - { value: "2.4%", label: "Logo churn (SMB-weighted)" }

  - kind: chart_insight
    title: Revenue grew 41% this year, with EMEA driving the Q4 step-up
    insight: Q4 acceleration reflects the EMEA launch landing ahead of schedule.
    source: Internal finance data, FY26 quarterly close
    chart:
      type: bar_chart
      title: Quarterly revenue ($M)
      data:
        categories: ["Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"]
        series:
          - name: Revenue
            values: [34, 40, 44, 48]
    insights:
      - Revenue grew 41% across the fiscal year, led by enterprise adoption.
      - The Q4 step-up reflects the EMEA market launch landing early.
      - Pipeline coverage points to continued acceleration into H2.

  - kind: decision
    title: Fund an SMB success pod in Q3 to protect 118% net retention
    recommendation: Stand up a dedicated SMB customer-success pod in Q3 to arrest churn before it compounds.
    options:
      - label: Hold current coverage
        detail: No new cost, and SMB churn keeps climbing through H2.
      - label: Fund an SMB success pod
        detail: Four people from Q3; protects net retention in the segment.
        recommended: true
      - label: Offshore SMB support
        detail: Cheapest per seat, at the expense of response time.

  - kind: closing
    title: Approve the SMB success pod this month
    subtitle: "Protects H2 growth · Owner: VP Customer Success · decision by 31 July"
